summary: 什翼犍之孙，代亡后复国，大会牛川即代王位，改称魏王；参合陂大破后燕、取并州、迁都平城称帝，离散部落、计口授田，北魏开国之基；晚年猜暴，天赐六年遇弑。
summary_en: Grandson of Shiyijian, he restored the state after Dai's fall, taking the throne at the Niuchuan assembly as King of Dai, then King of Wei; shattering Later Yan at the Canhe marshes, taking Bingzhou, and moving the capital to Pingcheng, he took the imperial throne, dissolved the tribes, and allotted land by mouth — the foundations of Northern Wei. In his last years jealous and cruel, he was slain in the 6th year of Tianci.

portrait.appearance_basis: 魏书载「帝隆准龙颜，目有精光」。画像宜表现开国雄主的英武之态，衣冠从北魏初制。属艺术想象。

timeline.title: 生
timeline.summary: 什翼犍孙，献明帝子。代亡后流寓。
timeline.summary_en: Grandson of Shiyijian, son of the late heir; he wandered after Dai's fall.

timeline.title: 即代王位
timeline.summary: 大会牛川，即代王位，旋改称魏王，北魏始。
timeline.summary_en: At the great assembly at Niuchuan he took the kingship of Dai, soon restyled King of Wei — the beginning of Northern Wei.

timeline.title: 参合陂之战
timeline.summary: 大破后燕慕容宝，坑降卒，国势陡升。
timeline.summary_en: He shattered Murong Bao of Later Yan, burying the surrendered alive — the state's power leapt upward.

timeline.title: 取并州
timeline.summary_en: He took Jinyang, Changshan, and the rest, reaching for Hebei.

timeline.title: 迁都平城称帝
timeline.summary: 迁平城，即皇帝位，定国号魏。
timeline.summary_en: He moved the capital to Pingcheng, took the imperial throne, and fixed the realm's name as Wei.

timeline.title: 遇弑
timeline.summary: 清河王绍弑帝，齐王嗣平乱即位。
timeline.summary_en: The Prince of Qinghe, Shao, slew the emperor; the Prince of Qi, Si, put down the rebellion and took the throne.

timeline.title: 离散部落
timeline.summary: 分土定居、计口授田等，鲜卑国家化关键。
timeline.summary_en: Allotting land by mouth and settling the tribes — the hinge of the Xianbei's passage to statehood.

relations.note_en: Restores the state after the fall of Dai and founds Northern Wei

relations.note: 天赐六年遇弑，长子嗣即位
relations.note_en: Assassinated in the sixth year of Tianci; his eldest son Si took the throne

bio_md:
# 道武帝 · 主要事迹

拓跋珪，什翼犍之孙。代国亡于前秦后，珪随母流寓。淝水之战前秦崩溃，拓跋珪乘机复国：登国元年大会牛川，即代王位，旋改称魏王——北魏之始。复国之初，珪「离散诸部，分土定居，不听迁徙」，又计口授田、劝课农桑，鲜卑部落联盟遂向国家转化，此北魏立国之本。

登国十年，珪率军与后燕慕容宝战于参合陂，大破燕军，坑杀降卒四五万人，后燕元气尽丧；皇始元年，克晋阳、取并州，拓地河北。天兴元年，迁都平城，即皇帝位，定国号魏——北魏之基业，至此奠定。珪又推行汉化之始：用崔浩等汉族士人，置博士、立大学，仿汉制设官。

然珪晚年「服寒食散，喜怒无常」，猜忌功臣，诛戮过甚；天赐六年，其次子清河王绍弑帝，年三十九。史评拓跋珪：「帝虽夷狄，而能任用贤能，开魏之基」；其复国开疆、部落国家化两事，为北魏一统北方奠定根基——北魏之兴，实自道武始。

> 参考：点校本《魏书》卷002《太祖纪》、卷001《序纪》。

bio_parts_en.value:
Tuoba Gui was the grandson of Shiyijian. When Former Qin destroyed the Dai state, Gui wandered with his mother. After the Fei River defeat broke Former Qin, he restored the state: at the great assembly at Niuchuan in the 1st year of Dengguo he took the kingship of Dai, soon restyled King of Wei — the beginning of Northern Wei. In the restoration he "dissolved the tribes, allotted them lands to settle, and forbade migration," and allotted land by mouth and urged farming — the passage of the Xianbei tribal league into a state, the very foundation of Northern Wei.

In the 10th year of Dengguo he met Murong Bao of Later Yan at the Canhe marshes, shattered the Yan army, and buried forty or fifty thousand prisoners alive — Later Yan never recovered; in the 1st year of Huangshi he took Jinyang and Bingzhou and reached for Hebei. In the 1st year of Tianxing he moved the capital to Pingcheng, took the imperial throne, and fixed the realm's name as Wei — the foundations of Northern Wei were laid. He also began the sinicization: with the Han gentry, Cui Hao and the rest, he established doctors and a grand academy and set the offices on the Han model.

But in his last years, "taking the cold-food powder, he was moody without measure," jealous of his meritorious ministers and slaying beyond reason; in the 6th year of Tianci his son, the Prince of Qinghe, Shao, slew him, aged thirty-nine. The historians say of him: "though a barbarian, he could employ the worthy and able, and opened the foundations of Wei" — the restoration, the conquests, and the making of the state were the root of Northern Wei's unification of the north.

> References: the punctuated critical edition of the *Weishu*, ch. 2 ("Benji of Emperor Daowu"), ch. 1 ("Prefatory Annals").
